title: Archimedean realisation and binding-trace commutativity
html:
Archimedean realisation & Trace Commutativity

Two independently defined binding traces — the exact active-partition factorization B_{\mathrm{sym}} and the Q-CLT statistical limit B_{\mathrm{qCLT}} — must land on the same macroscopic observable, and the standard-part map is what guarantees it. Here \mathcal{F}_{Arch} denotes the object-level standard-part map \mathrm{st} \colon \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} \to \mathbb{R} — a surjective ring homomorphism — applied to the real-valued binding traces; it is the underlying evaluation of the categorical standard-part functor \mathrm{St} (def:standard-part-functor), not a functor in its own right. It transforms algebraic traces into physical macroscopic observables, so that the evaluation of nuclear binding traces rigorously commutes as the scale A \to \infty. The payoff is already concrete in the tritium / helium-3 splitting: both routes agree that the n–n bond of tritium binds more tightly than the p–p bond of helium-3.

Numerical realization

The scale \alpha in the diagram is the canonical energy scale \alpha = E_0 = \mathfrak{m}_e/\bigl(q_0(q_0-1)\bigr), the electron mass lifted by the substrate factor — a derived quantity, not a free parameter (in particular it is neither the neutron \beta-decay value \mathfrak{Q}_\beta nor a deuteron-pinned fit). Writing the bond suppression s(K) = 1 - \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{atom}})/\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{free}}) and the log-ratio L(K) = \ln\bigl(\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{free}})/\mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{atom}})\bigr) = -\ln(1-s), the exact algebraic trace is B_{\mathrm{sym}} = \alpha\,L; its linearization B_{\mathrm{lin}} = \alpha\,s is the leading term of L = s + s^2/2 + \cdots and saturates at \alpha (since s < 1); and the Q-CLT limit B_{\mathrm{qCLT}} = \alpha \sum_i \ln|V_i| replaces the exact correlated trace by a sum of independent per-bond contributions, each V_i the Markov-trace ratio of a two-nucleon sub-braid. Taking every V_i equal to the deuteron bond gives the uniform limit; resolving the three bond types (p–p, p–n, n–n) by their own sub-braid ratios — with \ln|V_{n\text{-}n}| > \ln|V_{p\text{-}p}| — gives the factorized limit.

Evaluated on the light nuclei whose binding trace is canonical, the exact log-trace B_{\mathrm{sym}}(E_0) reproduces the measured binding within \approx 1.2\times for the non-anomalous A = 3 isotopes with no fit. The tritium / helium-3 splitting is resolved both by the exact trace and by the factorized Q-CLT: tritium carries an n–n bond where helium-3 carries a p–p bond, and the larger n–n sub-braid suppression makes tritium the more bound — a distinction the uniform-per-bond limit, blind to bond type, averages away. The doubly-magic ^4\mathrm{He}, which carries no single hyperbolic knot, is instead reproduced by the shell-closure specialization B = 2\,\mathfrak{m}_e\, A\,\mathrm{Vol}(L6a4) with \mathrm{Vol}(L6a4) = 8G the Borromean residue; the per-knot trace forms undershoot the heavier ^6\mathrm{Li} and ^7\mathrm{Li} by \approx 1.6\times, marking where the single-trace estimate gives way to shell structure. The side-by-side evaluation through this one canonical trace — now spanning ^2\mathrm{H} through ^7\mathrm{Li} — is recorded in binding-single-pipeline-comparison.witness.json.
